title: Calculate overall tumbling modes from diffusion tensor principal values — dxyz_dunit_to_overall_modes
text: Let \((D_x, D_y, D_z)\) denote principal values rotational diffusion tensor diffusion-frame principal-axis system. basis, rank-2 diffusion generator $$ \mathbf{L}^{(2)} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(D_x + D_y) & \sqrt{3}(D_x - D_y) & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{3}(D_x - D_y) & D_x + D_y + 4D_z & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & D_x + 4D_y + D_z & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4D_x + D_y + D_z & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & D_x + D_y + 4D_z \end{pmatrix}. $$ returned lambda_overall_vec contains negative decay rates associated distinct eigenvalues matrix, can combined negative internal-motion eigenvalues used elsewhere package. current implementation assumes dxyz_vec already ordered diffusion-frame convention generator . particular, axial-symmetry shortcut triggered \(D_x = D_y\), unique diffusion axis correspond z axis supplied diffusion frame. autocorrelation case currently implemented , dunit_b_matrix must equal dunit_a_matrix. row dunit_a_matrix interpreted average rank-2 unit dipole-dipole tensor diffusion frame. squared norm $$S^2 = \lVert \mathbf d^{\mathrm u} \rVert^2$$ used measure residual second-rank orientational order. S^2 = 1 corresponds orientational averaging, S^2 = 0 corresponds complete isotropic averaging rank-2 interaction. S^2 > s2_min, row normalized unit rank-2 direction projected onto overall tumbling eigenmodes. fully anisotropic diffusion, \(\hat{\mathbf d}\) normalized row \(\mathbf v_i\) orthonormal eigenvectors \(\mathbf{L}^{(2)}\), directional overall-mode weights $$a_{pi}^{\mathrm{dir}} = (\hat{\mathbf d}_p \cdot \mathbf v_i)^2.$$ eigenvectors orthonormal, directional weights sum one row: $$\sum_i a_{pi}^{\mathrm{dir}} = 1.$$ axially symmetric diffusion \(D_x = D_y\), generator already diagonal three grouped mode classes, directional weights reduce $$a_{p1}^{\mathrm{dir}} = \hat d_{p1}^2,$$ $$a_{p2}^{\mathrm{dir}} = \hat d_{p2}^2 + \hat d_{p5}^2,$$ $$a_{p3}^{\mathrm{dir}} = \hat d_{p3}^2 + \hat d_{p4}^2.$$ fully anisotropic diffusion, coupled \((Y_{2,0}, Y_{2,2}^{c})\) block diagonalized analytically.
